glosses: To increase in extent.
To possess a certain extent; to cover an amount of space.

examples.text: The desert extended for miles in all directions.

glosses: To cause to increase in extent.
To cause to last for a longer period of time.
To straighten (a limb).
To bestow; to offer; to impart; to apply.

examples.text: to extend sympathy to the suffering
to extend credit to a valued customer

glosses: To increase in quantity by weakening or adulterating additions.

examples.text: There's little stew left, but we can always extend it by adding more potatoes.
The skim milk and middlings should be mixed in a tub or barrel, and, if the supply of milk is short , it may be extended with water.

[…] the exalted morality of those virtuous brethren in the trade who, with consciences as weak as their own "extended" liquors, sought to convince him that to reduce the drink was a mercy to the poor deluded toper.

glosses: To value, as lands taken by a writ of extent in satisfaction of a debt; to assign by writ of extent.
Of a class: to be an extension or subtype of, or to be based on, a prototype or a more abstract class.

examples.text: The classes Person and Dog extend the class Animal.

glosses: To reenlist for a further period.

examples.text: Two years later, back to amtracs, this time at Camp Schwab, Okinawa, and I liked it so much I extended.

examples.text: Neue Schiebetüren lassen sich ganz leicht aufschieben.

glosses: etwas zeitlich verschieben

examples.text: Du musst endlich mit deinem Aufsatz beginnen. Du darfst es nicht weiter aufschieben.

glosses: etwas oder jemanden nach draußen schieben

examples.text: Und er wehrte sich mit Händen und Füßen, als der Mann ihn aus der Tür hinausschob, ein paar Stufen hinunter, bis in einen ganz engen, kleinen Raum, wo es stockfinster war, und …
Während nun die Wulschin ihr geängstigt Dirnlein zur Tür hinausschob und die Sibill zu beruhigen strebte, prüfte die Durl das Hemd der Toten.

glosses: etwas auf einen späteren Zeitpunkt verschieben

examples.text: Die Stiftung PWG versucht, Gesamterneuerungen so lang wie möglich hinauszuschieben und, wenn möglich, im bewohnten Zustand durchzuführen.
Abwarten und eine Sanierung hinauszuschieben werde nur die Maßnahme verteuern.
Es rechtfertigte ihn vor seinem Gewissen, wenn er einer verlorenen Tochter wegen die Entscheidung hinausschob.

glosses: To postpone, especially through procrastination.

examples.text: Don't put off your homework to the last minute.
Don't put your homework off to the last minute.
Don't put it off to the last minute.
Don't put it off.

glosses: To delay (a task, event, etc.).

examples.text: The storm put off the game by a week.
The storm put the game off by a week.
I'm too busy to see Mr Smith today. I'll have to put him off.

glosses: To distract; to disturb the concentration of.

examples.text: Please be quiet. I'm trying to concentrate and you're putting me off.

glosses: To cause to dislike; to discourage (from doing).

examples.text: Almost drowning put him off swimming.

glosses: To emit; to give off (an odor, smoke, etc.).

examples.text: This type of firewood puts off a strong smell.

glosses: To take off (something worn).

examples.text: to put off a mask

The power of turning into an animal has this serious disadvantage that it lays you open to the chance of being wounded or even slain in your animal skin before you have the chance to put it off and scramble back into your human integument.

glosses: offended, repulsed

examples.text: The guest was quite put off by an odor.

glosses: daunted or fazed

examples.text: All but the most dedicated were put off by the huge task.
